entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer for AI agents and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, available as a managed cloud service or Apache-2.0 self-hosted software. It supports semantic, keyword, and entity-based retrieval, with SDKs, a CLI, a self-hosted server, and a cloud platform.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight is an agent memory system built around long-term retain, recall, and reflect operations. It offers Python, Node.js/TypeScript, and Go clients and supports multiple LLM providers, including local options.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database and official Hermes Agent memory provider that organizes agent context as browsable files and directories. Its scoped search and retrieval use L0, L1, and L2 context-loading tiers.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee is an open-source memory platform that builds connected memory from documents, code, and conversations using a self-hosted knowledge graph engine. It supports local text processing without an LLM and includes a CLI for remembering and recalling text.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API, as well as an official Hermes Agent memory provider, that extracts facts and handles updates, contradictions, and forgetting. It offers connectors for services including Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, and GitHub, along with plugins, an MCP server, and JavaScript and Python API clients.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: gbrain is an opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent that stores sourced facts and supports corrections and withdrawal. Its memory can be shared across agents, with optional semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents that tracks peers, sessions, and messages over time. It supports managed, local, and self-hosted deployments and provides Python and TypeScript SDKs.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: ByteRover CLI treats memory as a Git repository, managing a context tree with Git-like commit, branch, and merge operations. It offers five-tier retrieval, including four non-LLM tiers, alongside a React/Ink TUI and REPL, support for 20 LLM providers, and 24 built-in agent tools.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a SQLite-backed memory layer for Hermes agents with one pure-Python dependency. It can integrate through MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK; its README reports BEAM results for v3.0.0 and notes that LongMemEval is pending.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto consolidates memories and reconciles conflicting information, then briefs agents with relevant memories before they act. It also supports importing and exporting memories through the Open Knowledge Format.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: memory-os is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent that includes vector search and structured facts. It uses local infrastructure with Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite, and applies a Ground Truth hierarchy to prioritize injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: Autocontext is a recursive self-improving context harness that helps agents tackle complex tasks by running tasks against evaluations. It keeps useful lessons, discards dead ends, and produces traces, reports, and playbooks.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: This Hermes Agent plugin uses a SQLite store and hierarchical DAG to persist messages. Its lcm_grep and lcm_recall tools help recover details from past context.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: Deja-vu indexes session histories from supported coding agents and searches across months of past work. A shared index supports session search and continuation in the terminal.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: This self-hosted Honcho backend enables private, cross-session memory for Hermes Agent. It supports OpenAI-compatible providers and local inference servers, with an automated setup script for Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: Signet provides a local-first layer for agent identity, memory, and secrets, with portable state across supported agent harnesses. It can import files, webpages, and conversations, and includes a dashboard for browsing memories and their sources.
entries.plur-ai/plur: Plur stores shared agent memory as plain-text YAML engrams on disk. It offers local search after a one-time model download, with keyword fallback; its README reports 95.6% R@5 on LongMemEval-S (N=500).
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: ClawMem is an on-device memory and context engine that combines BM25, vector search, rank fusion, and cross-encoder reranking. It can generate session handoffs and capture decisions and preferences, with integrations through hooks, MCP, and native agent plugins.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Sibyl-Memory keeps durable agent memory in a local SQLite file, using FTS5 search and a five-tier schema. Its package family includes an SDK, CLI, Hermes adapter, MCP server, and LangGraph BaseStore.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: ContextPilot optimizes context ordering for cache sharing, supporting text and multimodal context. Its context index handles reordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling, and it integrates with Hermes Agent and other listed runtimes.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: This Hermes memory plugin uses an embedded backend by default, with an HTTP backend also available. Recall results include a why_retrieved reason, and the plugin supports contradiction tracking and memory canonicalization.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: This agent-driven CLI maintains persistent, source-grounded knowledge as a Wiki with citations and history. It is designed to recall, maintain, and evolve memory across sessions without embeddings or a vector database.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: AgentCairn stores durable memory as inspectable Markdown files with frontmatter metadata, using an Obsidian vault as the source of truth. A local DuckDB cache supports hybrid search and retrieval, while MCP servers and host-specific plugins connect it to coding agents.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: Flowstate-qmd anticipates context needs by watching agent session logs and prefetching context into a cache. It uses local SQLite-vec storage and GGUF models via node-llama-cpp, and provides an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding agent clients.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack combines Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace under a single memory owner, using SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma for state and retrieval management. It provides the agent with a purpose-built evidence packet for each query.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: Keep builds reflective memory with semantic search that combines BM25 full-text search and ranked graph traversal. It can index codebases, URLs, and multimedia with OCR, while edge tags connect notes through navigable, bidirectional relationships.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: Hermes Tool Slimmer reduces tool-schema token use through local keyword-based ranking and Tool Search support. It integrates as middleware without patching Hermes core on version 0.19 or later, and includes a dashboard for tracking savings and managing tool configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: Agent Context OS provides a Git-backed context and workflow layer for Claude Code, Codex, and other listed compatible coding agents. Its workflows cover migration, handoffs, and memory proposals, with integrations that are opt-in rather than enabled automatically.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: This local-only Hermes memory plugin stores data in a single .lbdb embedded graph database file. Its retrieval combines BM25 keyword search with named graph relationships, and importance-weighted recall prioritizes high-priority memories during context prefetch.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: Hermes Local Knowledge indexes configured local sources and selected Hermes runtime sources for capability search and routing. It registers five tools for search, retrieval, traversal, feedback, and usage reports, along with three lifecycle hooks.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: Hermes AgentMemory is a pull-model episodic memory plugin with an on-demand summarizer and a trace.jsonl audit trace of prefetch operations. It supports immediate event deletion, so deleted events are not retained as persistent summaries.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/hermes-blind: Hermes Blind extracts the original goal from the first user turn of a long Claude Code or Codex session, with goals, first-sentence, and full extraction modes. It skips tool output and other non-user-turn records and uses neither a summarizing model nor an external service.
entries.piprail/piprail: Piprail provides a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets. It operates without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: Hermes XMemo provides durable cross-session memory with native lifecycle hooks for pre-turn recall and session-end snapshots. It uses a local SQLite layer for caching and write-outbox reliability, and can read memories from other connected agents.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: The Exabase plugin integrates Exabase M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It offers tools for searching and manually storing memories, with configurable query expansion and result reranking.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: SourceVault Code Tools provides private local code memory for repositories, with commands for search, file reads, context, and Q&A. It supports Hermes CLI, Telegram, and Hermes Desktop, and includes repository sync and indexed Git-history search commands.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes provides long-term memory for Hermes Agent, with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest enabled by default. It offers retrieval through HNSW ANN, sparse search, and an FM-index, and can run via native Rust FFI or an HTTP daemon.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield provides memory tools for Hermes Agent, including 17 tools for memory management and knowledge graph traversal. Its hybrid search combines BM25, vector, and graph methods, and it can checkpoint context automatically during message compression.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit helps curate agent memory stored as plain Markdown, proposing evidence-cited JSON diffs rather than requiring a database. Its rot and lint curators flag stale or conflicting facts, while a local Git repository tracks and can revert changes.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers provides composable skills and a software development workflow that guides agents through specification, design sign-off, planning, and subagent execution. It belongs on this list for its structured development methodology, with installation documented separately for multiple harnesses.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first design and prototyping system with skills, design templates, design systems, and plugins. Its support for coding agents through skills, CLI, MCP, or runtime adapters—including Hermes Agent—makes it a design-focused option for this list.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This project offers structured cybersecurity skills across security domains, mapped to frameworks including MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3. Its broad framework mappings and compatibility with more than 26 AI platforms make it a specialized security skills library.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: drawio-skill turns natural-language descriptions and real sources into editable .drawio files. Incremental sync preserves manual layout and annotations, while diagramctl and an optional MCP server provide ways to work with diagrams.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: internet-court-skill combines a master router and connector skills with vendored copies of official protocol skills. It also adds a verification and dispute-resolution layer for its agent-to-agent commerce workflows.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: avoid-ai-writing can score files or piped text for detectable AI writing patterns and rewrite content, with up to two editing passes. Its in-place editing mode refuses source code, configuration, and generated data.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw uses background evolution to deduplicate and improve skills, and unifies skill libraries across agents, devices, and team members. Its integrations include Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenAI-compatible APIs.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform library includes 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills for Claude Code and agents compatible with agentskills.io. It also maintains session state in the project's docs folder.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: pm-claude-skills provides professional agent skills, each with a framework, output template, and quality checks. Skills can be installed with the pm-claude-skills command, and the project is MIT-licensed.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: youtube-skills provides skills for transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction. It supports Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cursor, and requires a TranscriptAPI key with a 100-credit free tier.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: hermes-skill-factory watches active workflows for reusable patterns and proposes skills based on them. It can generate SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds, with slash commands to manage, list, and save detected patterns.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: super-hermes teaches Hermes Agent to generate custom thinking instructions for specific tasks and includes pre-built analytical lenses for various domains. Its reports pair findings with an account of analysis blind spots.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Adds type-safe agentskills.io support for Pydantic AI, including remote skill registries sourced from Git and S3. It also provides tools for accessing bundled resources and running scripts in a sandbox that isolates untrusted code from the host.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Turns rough ideas into structured design documents and implementation handoffs for Hermes Agent. Lite and Full modes suit different project complexities, while a PASS/FAIL review gate evaluates specs before handoff.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: Combines prose, diagrams, and source code in generated .lit.md files, then extracts runnable source files with a tangler. It also syncs edits to those source files back into the literate document.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: Supports long-running agent teams with shared coordination data stored in each repository’s Git root and defined work states and roles. Its plugins, recipes, and skills make it a distinct option for supervised team workflows.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Shares memory across instances through Markdown files and automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes. It also provides a pipeline for fine-tuning and switching to replacement models.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: A Portuguese-language Hermes Agent community project with skills in SKILL.md format and guides for installation, configuration, and use. Contributors can submit changes through forks and pull requests.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Provides prompting skills for FLUX image and video generation, alongside BFL API integration for polling and webhooks. Its FLUX 3 video suite includes eight specialist skills.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: Lists nine Chainlink skills that follow the Agent Skills specification, with installation available through `npx skills add smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills`. The README describes the repository as containing community examples only.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Creates agent instructions from repositories, documentation, and developer discourse as agentskills.io-compliant skills. It supports both automated and step-by-step workflows, with skill testing and export.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Nika describes a workflow language for AI with one file, four verbs, and one Rust binary. It checks workflows before calling a model, lets users choose the model, and verifies each run’s tamper-evident record.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: Provides a registry of reusable AI skills based on the AgentSkills specification, with both a Python client and a CLI. Its installation process resolves dependencies recursively, and it also includes TON-payment commerce features.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Supports autonomous execution of long-running, multi-step tasks with real-time tracking of progress and decisions. Checkpoints and built-in rollback procedures help recover safely when execution needs to be reversed.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: Manage Nextcloud files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts through WebDAV and CalDAV. It uses HTTPS with Nextcloud App Passwords and includes a guided setup script for validating credentials and configuring access.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: Browse, search, and install community skills through a hub built around the Agentic Resource Discovery v0.9 specification. It also offers federated search across GitHub and Hugging Face and is described as operating continuously via Hermes Agent on NVIDIA infrastructure.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Retrieve relevant skills through five layers, from hard triggers to semantic embeddings. By narrowing the skill list before LLM calls, it aims to reduce token usage, and it can degrade gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: This Claude Code skill creates reproducible demo GIFs for repository READMEs using VHS tape files or Playwright recording scripts, then optimizes GIFs for target sizes under 8 MB. It supports terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries, making it useful for projects that need README demos across different interfaces.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: This CLI and MCP server searches more than 13,870 MCP servers and 4,384 agent skills, and provides direct installation commands for discovered tools and plugins. Its support for MCP-compatible clients including Hermes makes it a discovery option for agents looking to find and install tools.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: This skill builds Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files, then validates them against runtime-specific profiles with CI-friendly exit codes. It also monitors official frontmatter specifications weekly to detect field drift, helping keep skills aligned with changing specifications.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: This host-agnostic feedback loop analyzes session history to identify skill coverage gaps and draft improvement proposals. Updates are gated by deterministic, LLM-judge, and regression evaluators, and it runs locally using Python’s standard library without daemons or external services.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: These Hermes Agent skills route file operations using the path syntax for native Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, and WSL environments. They also select and verify existing project-compatible Python interpreters, addressing two Windows runtime setup tasks.
entries.superagnt/leverage: Leverage provides agent skills for social data, CRM management, and lead enrichment, with support for Claude Code, Cursor, and other agentskills.io-compliant clients. It also includes an MCP server for browser-based OAuth authentication.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: This collection includes tools to transcribe Douyin videos into structured Markdown and SRT subtitles, remove common Chinese AI-writing patterns with a rule-based engine, and extract structured data from PDFs and images using macOS Vision. It brings video, writing, and document-processing tasks together in one set of Hermes skills.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: This Hermes Agent plugin lets agents list open support bounties, buy ticket context, and submit answers for review; a human approves the winning answer. It also provides public wallet earnings records and lets users create a bounty board with a URL, API key, and USDC deposit addresses.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: This skill automates USDC payments for HTTP 402 responses and supports Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols. It is compatible with OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and the agentskills.io standard.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: Skillseal tests agent skills in isolated Docker containers for structure, functionality, and security. It produces Ed25519-signed certificates that can be verified through its public API, which also accepts skill submissions.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Scavio for Hermes Agent provides structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server that exposes 191 tools. The project also includes five ready-to-use workflow skills and supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands.
entries.parkyucheol-del/alphapipeline: This remote MCP server provides quantitative risk and slippage tools for Polymarket L2 VWAP, on-chain DEX, and cross-venue arbitrage. Its token-risk tools return raw data rather than a safety verdict, and its x402 payments use USDC on Base.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: This skill generates Chinese news briefings at multiple geographic scales, from global coverage to street-level reporting. It structures reports around core conclusions and action suggestions, and uses semantic memory of user interests to expand searches.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: This project provides an MCP endpoint for Western and Vedic astrology with deterministic results and SHA-256 verifiable hashes. The endpoint requires no authentication, and supports per-call REST payments via x402 or MPP.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: A progressive MCP client that uses three-layer lazy loading to minimize token usage, with incremental discovery of server metadata and tool schemas. Its socket-based daemon architecture supports persistent connections, making it a distinct pick for Hermes Agent skills.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life_OS is an ADHD-friendly personal execution system for habits and study blocks, with agent-driven scheduling and system design through an MCP connection. It stands out for pairing that workflow with local storage in a single SQLite file and both a React web app and an Expo-based Android app.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard runs three parallel subagents to review code adversarially, focusing on edge cases, integration analysis, and other potential problems. It also uses a deterministic pre-scan and verifies findings with proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox; it is read-only and does not fix issues.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This Hermes Agent skill uses three parallel agents—Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness—to review code for simplification across TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust. Its tiered application process includes an approval gate, making it a distinct option for applying suggested code changes with review.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: A cybersecurity lab for Hermes Agent, with CVE-driven skills and tools for network work, forensics, and exploitation. It also integrates 28 cybersecurity frameworks and standards, making it a broad option for adding security-focused skills to Hermes.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: Fablize for Hermes adapts verified procedures for multi-story task decomposition, with mandatory evidence-based verification gates and safeguards against stopping early. It also provides a systematic protocol for reproduction and causal debugging, plus a Python goal engine for persistent task state management.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: A C#/.NET implementation of agentskills.io that uses SKILL.md files for progressive disclosure. It integrates with Microsoft.Extensions.AI for tool-based skill loading and can automatically register common agent skill directories, making it a practical option for adding skills to a Hermes agent.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is a local, real-time observability dashboard for Hermes Agent, tracking token costs, session history, skill analytics, and other activity such as cron jobs, channels, and incidents. It stands out for its read-only access and local log desensitization, with optional incident alerts through Telegram and Feishu.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: This project provides plain Markdown skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode, covering code review and session management workflows. Skills can be installed by copying a directory or using the bundled installer, making it a practical addition to a Hermes Agent skills list.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This project packages AI coding agents and development tools for Nix, including Hermes. Its README provides per-tool `nix run` commands, and the packages are automatically updated daily.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone collects scripts and notes for running agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent, on Android through Termux. It also documents OpenClaw configuration and access to hardware and UI features through Termux:API and Termux:GUI.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This Termux-based installer and guide runs Hermes Agent on Android using proot-distro Ubuntu. It supports interactive model setup, gateway services, shell command execution, and external providers or local models via Ollama.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This unofficial community Helm chart deploys Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with single-writer safeguards for persistent HERMES_HOME storage. It supports direct deployment or operator-ready CRD workflows, plus configurable gateway mode and optional API and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: This one-command installer brings the Hermes AI assistant to Android through Termux and to iOS through iSH. It also supports Telegram voice and file messaging, with scheduled tasks via cron jobs on Termux.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: hermesclaw runs Hermes Agent with hardware-enforced sandboxing through NVIDIA OpenShell. It restricts network and filesystem access at the kernel level and provides configurable policies for messaging and web search.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying, monitoring, and operating OpenClaw and Hermes agents on Docker or Kubernetes. It includes searchable logs, metrics, and alert rules, with access through a REST API, CLI, and MCP server.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image that includes mini-swe-agent and the official Hermes installation. It supports persistent state through mounted home directories and lets users build specific Hermes tags with build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This Nix package and NixOS module provides declarative Hermes deployment, including configuration for cli-config.yaml and workspace documents. It combines Nix-managed and CLI-installed skills and supports secrets integration through systemd EnvironmentFiles and sops-nix.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first control plane for operating multiple Hermes Agent instances from one web application, with separate workspaces and identities. It provides per-agent Telegram and WhatsApp channels and granular tool, path, and network permission policies.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes-OTG is a portable Hermes Agent package that runs from a USB drive or other drive without host installation or registry writes. It includes Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes with isolated data environments, and bundles tools for offline use.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: This project sets up Hermes Gateway as a reboot-safe systemd service for headless Ubuntu and Debian servers. It supports autonomous execution of recurring AI cron jobs and integrates with Nous Portal.
entries.jyje/hermes-agent-helm: This Helm chart deploys Hermes Agent on Kubernetes and can be installed from an OCI registry or a GitHub Pages Helm repository. Optional Copilot and Codex device-login bootstrap and CI tests on an ephemeral kind cluster make it a Kubernetes-focused deployment option.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents is a multi-agent framework for financial trading research, with analysts covering fundamentals, sentiment, news, and technical signals. It is intended for research, not trading advice.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control provides self-hosted orchestration for assigning tasks, registering agents, browsing memory, and tracking costs. It offers Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API interfaces, with local Node.js installation or Docker deployment.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires is a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent and several other agents. It supports persistent tmux sessions, Git worktrees, and multi-repository workspaces; its web dashboard includes terminal access and diffs.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: Hermes Agent Control Room is a template for scaling Hermes Agent from a single VPS agent to specialist teams and automated workflows. Its level-based architecture includes a task bus for delegation and handoffs, plus skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: Swarmclaw helps build autonomous agent swarms, with support for 23+ LLM providers, durable agent memory, and MCP tool integration. Visual org charts show how work is delegated across agent teams.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions is a Mission Control interface for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work. It tracks tasks and review queues on a Kanban board, streams agent reasoning and tool execution, and requires human verification of agent-proposed completions.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized agents across research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. A Master Orchestrator routes and coordinates work through a strict pipeline architecture.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local web system for collaboration among agents built on Hermes Agent profiles, MCP, ACP, and Hermes Kanban. Leader and Specialist agents manage task lifecycles, while a real-time Web UI shows agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: Hermes Agent Metaharness automates outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code. It coordinates TBLite and TerminalBench-2 evaluations and provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator stages a competition between two AI companies, orchestrating nine autonomous agents for task execution and learning with Paperclip and Hermes Agent. Its real-time dashboard visualizes agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel runs a local Mixture-of-Agents stack that queries models in parallel and synthesizes their responses, using Hermes for task routing and tool-calling. It is designed for consumer GPUs, optimized for RTX 4080/5080 hardware, and described as having no cloud dependencies.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph builds a full project graph with `codegraph init`, using structural extraction and cross-file resolution for supported languages. Its MCP support makes that pre-indexed code knowledge available to Hermes Agent and other coding agents, with the stated goal of reducing token usage and tool calls.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale tracks token usage across AI coding agents, including Hermes, Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, and Gemini. Its terminal interface and visualization dashboard help users review usage, and it can submit usage data to a leaderboard.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap is a local trace viewer for coding-agent API traffic, including Hermes Agent requests. It lets users inspect prompts, tool calls, streaming responses, and token usage, compare adjacent requests for context changes, and redact common auth headers before recording traces.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor displays token usage, costs, and rate limits in real time, reading Hermes Agent state alongside other command-line tools. It tracks usage across 46+ AI coding tools, with historical trends, usage breakdowns, and multi-device sync.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design systems and layout guidance through MCP servers for building UI with AI. It is compatible with any AI provider supporting markdown or general prompting and integrates with Hermes Agent, Cursor, Claude, and GitHub Copilot.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes adds an opinionated workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent. It includes skills for product briefs, design handoffs, and implementation, plus seven agents for roles across the product lifecycle; its GitHub integration can enable issue and pull request delivery.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins is a community CLI for customizing the Hermes terminal UI, including banner colors, spinners, and ASCII art banners. YAML-based configuration supports theme creation, with examples ranging from retro DOS to cyberpunk aesthetics.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang is a command-line static linter for AI agent configurations, tool descriptions, and system prompts, with HERM v1.1 scoring. It scans prompts, tool definitions, schemas, and agent files, then reports findings with specific fixes and supported line references.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place describes itself as a social economy for autonomous AI agents. It provides encrypted agent-to-agent messaging via Signal Protocol, identity registration with human-readable @handles, and commerce using Solana-based USDC and SOL payments.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser for autonomous agent control via MCP, with support for Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and other AI providers. A supervisor sidebar manages agent approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads, and the browser supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes-CCC ports the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to Claude Code Channel. It runs natively in Claude Code without separate processes or OAuth and includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages with two tiers: a permanent knowledge graph and a session cache. Its Claude Code plugin auto-captures and auto-recalls context.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: This setup combines RTK and Caveman templating for workflows it says can save 90–99% of tokens. It also bundles 40+ preconfigured skills for finance, DevOps, and research, with automated installation for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: Ankh.md provides per-folder configuration and skills for creating scoped Hermes Agents, including project-local memories, tools, and custom instructions. It switches between the default agent and scoped agents, making it useful for keeping project-specific setups separate.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: evey-setup automates installation of hermes-agent and 12+ supporting services, with three deployment tiers ranging from a minimum viable setup to a production stack. It also supports 29 community plugins across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: This tool migrates OpenClaw data—including SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, and memory archives—to Hermes. It also maps configurations and credentials to Hermes YAML and JSON formats and can set up systemd gateway services.
entries.observeco/observeco: observeco is a Hermes plugin that exports real-time telemetry from agent conversations and monitors multi-agent systems in passive or scheduled active-probing modes. Its config-aware baselines are designed to detect performance drift relative to local file changes.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: hermes-voice adds voice interaction to Hermes Agent, with support for 35 languages via Piper and 9 via Kokoro. It runs offline without API keys or accounts and includes adaptive turn-taking and barge-in.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: hermes-startup is a local runtime for pursuing online opportunities, operating deterministically with zero network access by default. It requires explicit approval for consequential actions and external writes, and includes contracts for opportunities, offer previews, and exact approvals.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: hermes-memoss is a MemOS memory plugin with semantic search and multidimensional memory storage. It includes tools to search, add, and delete memories, plus a circuit breaker for MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: A cross-platform manager for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Gemini CLI, and Hermes Agent. It lets users switch API providers in one click and manage MCP, Skills, and Prompts in one place.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: A local, open-source cowork app for Hermes Agent and other agent CLIs, with a built-in agent that offers file access, web search, and MCP tools. It includes 21 ready-to-use assistants and supports macOS, Windows, and Linux.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: A web interface for using Hermes Agent from a browser or phone, organized into panels for chat, sessions, and workspace files. It also offers profiles, settings, session tools, and themes, with remote access available through an SSH tunnel.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: A desktop companion for installing, configuring, and chatting with Hermes Agent using the official Hermes install script. Its GUI manages profiles, sessions, skills, and tools, and the app is available from the project website or GitHub Releases.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: A Hermes Agent dashboard for multi-platform AI chat, session management, scheduled jobs, usage analytics, and channel configuration. It supports shared chats, group chat, visual workflows, persistent sessions, and tools for files, voice, devices, and agent management; desktop apps are available for Windows, macOS, and Linux, as well as npm and Docker distributions.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: A web workspace that brings together chat, a terminal, a memory browser, a skills manager, and an inspector panel. It also includes Swarm Mode with role-based dispatch and tmux-backed workers, plus a file browser with Monaco and a PTY terminal.
entries.spacering-net/codeg: A collaborative multi-agent coding workspace that aggregates sessions from Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and other agents as a desktop or self-hosted app. Users can search and resume sessions, hand them to another agent, or delegate and queue tasks in separate worktrees.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: A native Mac workspace for Hermes that connects directly to local or SSH hosts and works with real session data. It provides views for sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs, along with an embedded terminal for shell access and system repair.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: A Windows-first Chinese desktop app for Hermes Agent, with support for Windows and macOS and native window and process management. It includes a built-in Hermes-CN-Core kernel with health checks and updates, plus interfaces for chat, memory management, and LaTeX/Markdown rendering.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: A Chromium side-panel extension that connects the active browser context to a local or remote Hermes Agent runtime. It can capture page context and selected-tab screenshots, and its Bot Mode supports agent switching and group chats.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: A native SwiftUI iPhone client for driving a self-hosted Hermes agent, paired with a hermes-webui server that you run yourself. It supports iOS 18+ and is free, with no analytics or tracking.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: A desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, plus custom LLM model routing. It includes a runtime dashboard for token usage and latency and a live workspace for monitoring code writes and diffs.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is an interactive TUI with nine tabs and four selectable color themes. It tracks agent growth, Git projects, and scheduled cron jobs, and includes a tmux operator view for managing live agent panes.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: Agent Sessions is a native macOS browser and cockpit for sessions from Hermes agents and other coding-agent CLIs. It lets you search prompts, responses, tool activity, errors, and file paths, then resume supported sessions in Terminal.app, iTerm2, or Warp; session history stays on the Mac with no telemetry.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: Hermes Control Interface is a self-hosted web dashboard for the Hermes AI agent stack, bringing a browser-based terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and agent status panel together. It also offers streaming chat with tool-call visualization, an MCP server control plane, and a ZOO Swarm Monitor for agent health and kanban pipelines.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: Hermes Desktop OS1 is a native macOS workspace for Hermes Agent on Orgo cloud VMs and SSH hosts. It includes one-click Hermes Agent installation on fresh cloud computers and integrated WebRTC voice mode using OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: Hermes Agent Mission Control is a self-hostable dashboard template that connects a local Hermes agent to web dashboards through a Postgres message bus. Its approval inbox handles requests with side effects, making it a fit for workflows that need a review step.
entries.liftaris/herm: Herm is an alternative Hermes TUI and dashboard built with OpenTUI, combining chat and session management with a kanban board for agentic work. It also provides controls for profiles, skills, cron jobs, and toolsets.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: Hermes Telegram MiniApp is a locally run, mobile-first React SPA dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0. It offers terminal chat with streaming responses and file attachments, Telegram authentication using HMAC-SHA256 and Ed25519, and background agent spawning for up to five concurrent instances.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: Portable Hermes Agent is a desktop version for Windows that requires no installation, Docker, or admin rights. It includes 100 tools across 20+ toolsets, supports cloud AI and local models through LM Studio, and provides a workflow engine with scheduling, conditions, loops, and parallel execution.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: Hermes UI is a self-hosted web interface with a glassmorphic design for chat and real-time log streaming. Its file browser and task tracking dashboard sit alongside tools for managing skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI is a process-monitoring and configuration dashboard for Hermes, with real-time session activity and cost tracking. It also supports inspection of conversation histories and skill source code, plus read-only monitoring of configuration and environment variables.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: Pan-UI is a self-hosted AI workspace centered on chat, with real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards. It includes a marketplace for discovering and installing skills and MCP servers, as well as isolated profiles for separate sessions, memory, and API keys.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: Hermes Agent Desktop is a native desktop client for multi-agent collaboration, with streaming SSE responses and model switching. It pairs an orchestrator for 20 specialized AI agents with a visual Skill Store offering 50+ curated one-click installations.
entries.robbyczgw-cla/hermes-ui-plus: An unofficial, open-source interactive chat client for self-hosted Hermes Agent, with answers that can include checklists, choices, forms, and rankings. It also lets you approve or deny commands from your phone and runs on Android, web, macOS, and Linux alpha.
